dehydrated_text:
And what's going to happen here is in heaven there's going to be a conversation between Dante and Beatrice, who he loves. They're going to discuss the nature of the universe. The greatest gift from God as He created was freedom of the world, which He values most.

So the underlying principle of the universe is freedom of will. If God is love, then He must trust people. Therefore, freedom—freedom of will—is the most important principle. Same thing if you're a parent—if you truly love your child, you will let them go and make their own mistakes. You will not protect them, even if it means they might get kidnapped or whatever.

Brother, this ordinance is buried from the eyes of everyone whose intellect has not matured within the flame of love. So Peter is saying to Dante that this makes no sense because you're thinking with your mind, but the mind is not where the spark is; the divine spark is in the heart. Stop thinking with your mind and feel with your heart, letting the divine spark glow in you.

God's godliness has banished every envy from its own self, burning in itself and sparkling in the soul, showing eternal beauties. All that derives directly from this godliness is everlasting because God is perfect—forever good, forever love, compassion, and forgiveness. There's a spark of God in us, our hearts, meaning perfection always exists within us.

Even though the spark is forever in us, we can cover it up with mud or dirt by forgetting about it through evil deeds and disobedience. The more evil we do, the more we forget the spark, dimming it in us. The spark can glow or dim depending on our actions but will always be there.

Parents' true love is to trust their kids, letting them make mistakes. If your child is in danger, you go save them, but fear and anxiety shouldn't destroy their freedom. You need to let your child feel the anxieties but also do what they want, like going to play in the playground. Sending a child to the playground where there are other children and adults around is safe; sending them outside at midnight to one of the streets is not.

Man cannot regain his dignity unless he fills emptiness with just man's evil pleasure. The problem is that we do all this evil, can't forgive ourselves, and get stuck where we are.
